report:
Reassessed the complete claim and the sole implementation/test associations from the captured inputs. Producer or keyed-lookup reexecution after a coarse input change is permitted, including unrelated edits; it is not itself a violation. The obligation is that an equal semantic result backdates and prevents expensive downstream consumer invalidation. The implementation TODO in service_spec.rs explicitly leaves the complete guarantee unestablished, mentioning selected backdating and coarse same-file reexecution. I accept that as a declared coverage/implementation gap, not evidence that the selected behavior works or that coarse reexecution must be eliminated.

The complete associated test set is the single todo::crates_sage_ir_crate_reexecution_and_invalidation function. Its body contains no executable assertion. Its prerequisite is to associate and review real edit tests distinguishing which producers/lookups execute, semantic keyed-value equality/change, and expensive consumer reuse for unchanged, relevant, and unrelated edits. This accounts for both the equality/backdating guarantee and the qualification permitting upstream work. Those experiments and complete implementation evidence remain deferred; no implemented or tested guarantee is awarded to the empty placeholder. No N/A or ordinary evidence is present. No additional edits are required for this explicit deferral.

Baseline verification: independently compared both historical implementation_sources and test_sources against the current service_spec.rs and confirmed exact byte equality. The prior rationale remains sufficient as a TODO assessment, with its test matrix interpreted as planned assertions, not executed tests. Assessment uses only the current captured claim, whole implementation file, test body and metadata; no extra behavior dependencies were relied on. Execution: ran review start and the byte comparisons; no tests/build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator-reported 321 functional tests and root build are separate execution evidence and do not establish this deferred claim.
